items.q: Complete the pathogenesis flowchart of hypertension and pulmonary oedema in PSGN — 1) NAPlr + plasmin  2) ENaC  3) Na⁺ and H₂O retention … A) Epithelial sodium channel that is activated  B) End result: hypertension and pulmonary oedema  C) Activates the channel
items.exp: Flowchart: NAPlr + plasmin → activates ENaC (epithelial Na⁺ channel) → retention of Na⁺ and H₂O → hypertension and pulmonary oedema. (Book p776)

items.q: The channel activated by the NAPlr–plasmin complex in PSGN is:
opts: ROMK — the renal outer medullary potassium channel
items.exp: NAPlr + plasmin activates ENaC (epithelial Na⁺ channel), causing sodium and water retention that explains hypertension and pulmonary oedema. (Book p776)

items.q: Fill up: NAPlr bound to ______ activates ENaC in PSGN.
items.exp: NAPlr + plasmin activates the epithelial Na⁺ channel (ENaC). (Book p776)

items.q: In PSGN, volume-dependent hypertension and pulmonary oedema are attributed to ENaC-mediated retention of sodium and water.
opts: False — they result from low oncotic pressure alone
True, but only after 8 weeks of disease
False — ENaC activation causes sodium loss
items.exp: The pathogenesis chart links NAPlr-plasmin → ENaC activation → Na⁺/H₂O retention → hypertension and pulmonary oedema. (Book p776)

items.q: Renal function tests in PSGN typically show:
opts: Severe renal failure needing dialysis in most
items.exp: Basic investigations: RFT shows mild impairment, matching the reversible oliguric picture of PSGN. (Book p776)

items.q: A 6-year-old with PSGN has the following urinalysis: RBCs 3+, albumin 1+, and white cell casts on microscopy. This picture is:
opts: Typical of PSGN — ↑↑ RBC with 1+/2+ albumin and WBC casts
Typical of nephrotic syndrome — 4+ albumin with fatty casts
Typical of acute interstitial nephritis — sterile pyuria with WBC casts only
Typical of acute tubular necrosis — muddy brown granular casts
items.exp: Urine examination in PSGN: ↑↑ RBC, albumin 1+/2+, and WBC casts. (Book p776)

items.q: A child with PSGN has a persistently low C3 beyond 8 weeks. The book's stated action is:
opts: Reassure without investigation — C3 takes 6 months to recover
Repeat the ASO titre and treat with penicillin
Start empirical steroids for nephrotic syndrome
items.exp: Biopsy indication: ↓C3 persisting beyond 8 weeks — likely C3 GN (serum C3 normally normalises by 8 weeks in PSGN). (Book p776)

items.q: A second episode of post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis is common and simply needs a repeat course of penicillin.
opts: False — PSGN does not recur, so a recurrence needs evaluation for an alternative diagnosis
True — recurrence is expected within 8 weeks of the first episode
True, but recurrence occurs only after a streptococcal skin infection
False — recurrence means the child requires immediate dialysis
items.exp: Biopsy indication 2: recurrent episode — PSGN does not recur, hence an alternative diagnosis must be evaluated. (Book p776)

items.q: The histopathology of PSGN is best described as:
opts: Diffuse proliferative GN with exudative neutrophilic capillary infiltration exceeding mesangial proliferation
Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis with podocyte effacement
Membranous nephropathy with spike-and-dome subepithelial deposits
Mesangioproliferative GN with isolated mesangial IgA
items.exp: Histopathology in PSGN: DPGN (diffuse proliferative GN) with exudative neutrophilic capillary infiltration > mesangial proliferation. (Book p776)

items.q: Fill up: The histopathology of PSGN is abbreviated DPGN, i.e. diffuse ______ glomerulonephritis.
items.exp: DPGN = diffuse proliferative glomerulonephritis, with neutrophils in capillary loops exceeding mesangial proliferation. (Book p776)

items.q: Match the immunopathology with its PSGN phase — 1) Clinical phase on immunofluorescence  2) Recovery phase on immunofluorescence  3) Electron microscopy … A) Subepithelial camel-hump deposits  B) Granular IgG ± C3 in capillary walls > mesangium  C) Only C3 in the mesangium
items.exp: IF: clinical phase = granular IgG ± C3 in capillary walls more than mesangium (starry sky); recovery phase = only C3 (mesangial). EM: subepithelial camel-hump (lumpy bumpy) deposits. (Book p776)

items.q: A renal biopsy from a child in the recovery phase of PSGN is stained for immunofluorescence. Which deposit pattern is expected now?
opts: Granular IgG ± C3 along capillary walls
Linear IgG along the glomerular basement membrane
No deposits at any phase of PSGN
items.exp: Recovery phase IF: only C3 (mesangial); the granular IgG + C3 capillary-wall pattern belongs to the clinical phase. (Book p776)
